'''Yamazue Shrine''' (山末神社) is a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|en|Setsumatsusha|qid=Q1071160|lt=branch shrine}} of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Outer Shrine) within the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}} complex. It holds the 13th position among the 16 branch shrines of the Outer Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929), pp. 9, 12.</ref>

== Overview ==

Located within the precincts of the Outer Shrine in {{ill|Toyokawachō|ja|豊川町 (伊勢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokawa, Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17223204}}, {{ill|Ise, Mie|en|Ise, Mie|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise, Mie}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}.<ref name="uy">Compiled by Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.12</ref> It is situated at the southeastern edge of {{ill|Takakurayama (Ise)|ja|高倉山 (伊勢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Takakura (Ise)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11668768}} within the shrine grounds.<ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.59</ref> However, it is not directly connected to the Outer Shrine’s main approach path, requiring visitors to exit the precinct before entering again. Further south of {{ill|Yamazue Shrine|ja|山末神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamazue Shrine|qq=}} are the {{ill|Tanoe-Ōmizu Shrine|ja|田上大水神社・田上大水御前神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanoe-Ōmizu Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.38</ref>

The enshrined deity is Ōyama-tsu-hime no Mikoto (大山津姫命),<ref name="ic"/> revered as the mountain deity ({{ill|Yama-no-Kami|ja|山の神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yama-no-kami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q839254}}) of the Outer Shrine’s sacred rice fields and the deity of the spring that irrigates them.<ref name="ic"/> These sacred rice fields were once known as "Toyomiyasaki no Mita," sprawling across the area south of Yamasue Shrine,<ref name="gk"/> though the land has since been urbanized.<ref name="ic"/> In *Ise Province Shrine Name Register Commentary* by Watarai Nobunori, the enshrined deity is referred to as "Ōyamakui no Kami, also known as Yamasue no Ōnushi no Kami." Ōyamakui no Kami (大山咋神) appears in the *{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}*, symbolizing the deification of sacred mountains.<ref name="sk9">Compiled by the Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p.349</ref>

The shrine structure is of {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} style with a {{ill|Wood shingle|ja|板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ita-buki|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=杮葺|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q199388}} (wooden shingle) roof, surrounded by a {{ill|Sacred fences|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=Tamagaki}} (sacred fence).<ref name="sk1">Compiled by the Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p.351</ref> A single {{ill|Torii|ja|神明鳥居|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei torii|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=鳥居|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q234731}} stands, measuring 8 shaku 3 sun (approximately 2.5 meters) in height.<ref name="sk1"/> Interestingly, the torii does not face the shrine’s approach but is positioned toward a stone wall. No offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/saisenbako|qid=Q135491444}}) is provided.

== History ==

The name "山末神社" (Yamasue Shrine) refers to its location at the end (末) of Mt. Takakura, where "末" indicates the summit rather than the base of the mountain.<ref name="ic"/> In documents such as the "{{ill|Engi Ise Daijingu-shiki|ja|延喜伊勢太神宮式|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi Ise Daijingu-shiki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}" and the "{{ill|Enryaku Gishikichō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyuke Daijingu Gishikicho|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=延暦儀式帳|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q109596938}}", it is written as "山末社".<ref name="sk9"/>

Based on the definition of auxiliary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, it was established before the compilation of the "{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}" in 927 (Enchō 5). Additionally, since it is mentioned in the "Toyuke Daijingu Gishikicho," it must have existed prior to 804 (Enryaku 23). Although "{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|qq=}}" does not directly mention the founding of Yamasue Shrine, it describes how Yamatohime-no-mikoto viewed the area from Yamasue while searching for a suitable location for the shrine.<ref name="sk9"/>

Rituals ceased by the end of the medieval period, and the shrine's location became unknown during the early modern period. However, through the efforts of the Chief Priest {{ill|Kiyonaga Kawabe|ja|河辺精長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Kiyoshige|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q92924151}}, the shrine was restored at its current site on June 23, 1663 (Kanbun 3, Julian calendar: July 27, 1663).<ref name="sk0">Shikinaisha Kenkyukai (1990): p.350</ref> During its restoration, references from "{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei Hisho|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}" indicating "Yamasue Shrine, located in Miyama, Ohnashi Valley, south of Mitaguchi Shrine, Tsugihashi-go" were consulted for field surveys.<ref name="sk0"/>

The shrine was reconstructed on January 1, 1921 (Taisho 10),<ref name="uy"/> and again in July 1957 (Showa 32), with major renovations carried out on October 27, 1983 (Showa 58).<ref name="sk1"/>

== Rituals ==

The following rituals are performed by a group of three priests: Gon-negi, Miyakujou, and Shutsushi, in a巡回祭典 (巡回 ritual) format:
* {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai}} (February 20)
* {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June 20 and December 20)
* {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}} (October 20)
* {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}} (November 26)

Remote rituals (遥祀) are conducted for:
* {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}} (January 1)
* {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai|qq=}} (January 3)
* National Foundation Day Festival (February 11)
* {{ill|Kazahi-no-Misai|ja|風日祈祭|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|qid=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524493}} (May 14 and August 4)
* {{ill|The Emperor's Birthday|ja|天長祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenchō-sai|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=天皇誕生日|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q72318}} (December 23)<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyukai (1990): p.352</ref>

== Access ==

; To Gekū (Outer Shrine)
* **By Train:** Approximately 5-minute walk from JR {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangu Line}} or Kintetsu {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Yamada Line}} Ise-shi Station (south exit, JR side) via Gekū Sando.<ref>Ise Bunka Publishing (2008): p.33</ref>
* **By Bus:** About 5 minutes on foot from Mie Kotsu's "Ise-shi Station" bus stop.
* **By Car:** About 5 minutes north from Ise-Nishi IC on the Ise Expressway via Mie Prefectural Route 32. Parking is available nearby with a capacity of 448 cars.<ref>Jingu Administration Office "[http://www.isejingu.or.jp/mobile/i/parking/index.html Parking Information]" (accessed September 15, 2013)</ref>

; From Gekū to Yamasue Shrine
From Gekū, head south along Mikumoto Road (御木本道路) adjacent to the Jingu Forest, turn left at the site of the former Toyomiya-zaki Bunko (豊宮崎文庫), and ascend moss-covered stone steps to reach {{ill|Watarai Okunitama-hime Shrine|ja|度会大国玉比賣神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai Okunitama-hime Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Igari Shrine|ja|伊我理神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Igari Shrine|qq=}}, and {{ill|Igari Shrine|ja|井中神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inaka Shrine|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=伊我理神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11379372}}.<ref>Ise Bunka Publishing (2008): pp.37-38</ref> Continuing approximately 500 meters further along the forest will lead to Yamasue Shrine.<ref name="ic"/>
